rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the theorem display, the exponent begins directly with the opening parenthesis and n; there is no separate 2 before it. It reads H^{(n-i)+1} (crops/14_scan038_L256_theorem_degree.jpg). In the curve display there is a clear leading 2, while the final digit has hooked upper and lower turns, favoring 3; the existing 3|1 doubt remains appropriate (crops/14_scan038_L256_curve_degree.jpg). The first display independently and clearly reads H^{2(n-i)+1}, including both its leading 2 and terminal straight 1 (crops/14_scan038_L256_initial_degree.jpg).
rows.note: Author's slips or a proposed mathematical correction, not grounds to replace the literal exponents by the uniform intended degree. Written: H^{(n-i)+1} in the theorem, and H^{2(n-i)+3} favored in the curve display, retaining the exact existing \unsure{3|1} because that final digit is not fully decisive. Intended in both: H^{2(n-i)+1}. With the supplied correspondence degree shift 2i-2n, requiring output degree 1 gives d+2i-2n=1, hence d=2(n-i)+1; this agrees with the page's initial display. The candidate is byte-for-byte unchanged. Main should settle only whether the curve's current 3|1 doubt can be narrowed; it must not be silently changed to 1 solely for degree consistency.
rows.event_type: used and rechecked in this run
rows.event_outcome: Visually collated the full scan and three separate enlarged, contrast-raised exponent crops. Confirmed the omitted leading 2 in the theorem and retained the existing curve-digit doubt. The separate algebraic degree calculation is recorded as its own event.
rows.uncertainty_note: After inspection by both readers, the terminal numeral in the curve exponent remains 3|1; the existing in-place doubt is retained. The theorem display definitely omits the leading factor 2.

additional_events.outcome: Degree-consistency calculation only, conditional on the supplied shift 2i-2n: solving d+2i-2n=1 gives d=2(n-i)+1. This does not verify the correspondence theorem or justify changing the manuscript ink.
